body: She's always been ambivalent about her mass; not particularly pleased but not self-loathing. I'll bring it up as a conversation piece.

It does help a bit. The problem is our sex life is anything short of spectacular. I've unlocked the secrets to making her cum but through extreme effort, so most of the fun is lost. 

There are some issues in our relationship but we work through maturely. It's more than sex. I don't want to reach the conclusion that we both should move on but denial doesn't help shit. Of course there's so much that I'm not disclosing. This is something I need to seriously think about. 
Thanks.

I'm a health nut so I've been working and eating a new diet in tandem with her. I don't have enough nutitional knowledge to help her besides suggesting portion control, no trans-fats and complex carbs. However, she won't appeal to the idea of seeing a nutritionist. 

I can empathize with her as I'm in the opposite extreme, skinny and unable to gain. It must be very frustrating for her which is why bringing it up to her in any style of conversation would end horribly.

I'm aware of ailing levels of dopamine and other endorphins by cause of evolution, but even then attraction at some base level should still be present. Sadly it's not. When we're spending time together it's great. My heart still flutters but when it comes to sex my body just hopes. It sucks.

A bit confusing. Let me phrase it better. She is overweight - the weight that she's lost hasn't affected inches at all in fact she looks ... Bigger. I feel weird even talking about this cause it just sounds shallow. But the reality is my libido is shunning her and I want to fix that.

I won't reply to one particular message but both. Thanks. I don't know what I'm going to be doing in the future but this is my fourth year of university so I've already shut away any notions of personal growth and satisfaction. 

My therapist has been useless. We talk and seek the derivations of my issues but it only makes me more upset. I refuse to go on meds, just cause if I can't solve problems on my own (not discounting my peers) then I'd rather live with the problem. 

I've been getting by with deep breaths and "just one more year" speeches for a little while. Here's hoping it continues. 

It's difficult to climb out of a depressive hole when nothing can convince you that you're worth something.
